title: Git attribution: emit deduped commit_meta dictionary keyed by commit_id
description:
## Context
After wiring `commit_id` into finding events, repeating commit metadata on every finding wastes bytes and CPU (OID hex formatting, repeated serialization). `scanner-rs` already has O(1) commit metadata lookup via `CommitGraphIndex`.

Relevant primitives:
- `CommitGraphIndex::commit_oid()` and `CommitGraphIndex::committer_timestamp()` (`src/git_scan/commit_graph.rs`).
- Existing finding event already carries `commit_id` (`src/unified/events.rs`).
- Existing lock-free dedupe primitive: `AtomicBitSet` (`src/stdx/atomic_bitset.rs`).

## Goal
Add a deduped commit metadata side channel/table keyed by `commit_id` so findings stay compact while still exposing commit OID/time.

## Scope
- Introduce a `commit_meta` event/table emitted once per commit ID encountered in findings.
- Include at least:
  - `commit_id` (u32 graph position)
  - `commit_oid` (raw bytes or canonical hex representation)
  - `committer_timestamp` (u64 epoch seconds)
- Keep finding events compact (do not duplicate OID/time per finding).

## Performance Constraints
- Emit-once guarantee under concurrency using atomic bitset gating.
- O(1) lookup from commit_id -> metadata via precomputed arrays.
- Avoid per-finding OID formatting and repeated allocation.
- Keep serialization in manual writer path; avoid introducing dynamic JSON alloc churn in hot loop.
- Target regression: statistically insignificant at repo-scale (<1-2%), with p50/p95 checks.

## Data-Structure/Algorithm Notes
- Dense membership: atomic bitset sized to `CommitGraphIndex::len()`.
- Metadata storage: SoA-leaning representation for cache locality (packed OIDs + timestamp vecs; avoid scattered heap objects).
- Sink path should accept dictionary-style metadata emission for downstream join by `commit_id`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every commit ID appearing in findings has exactly one matching `commit_meta` emission.
- No duplicate `commit_meta` under parallel scanning.
- Findings remain compact and reference commit metadata by ID.
- JSONL/text/sarif behavior documented for new metadata channel.
- Perf evidence included: before/after throughput and output size deltas.
notes:
Research refinement (implementation-critical):
- Add explicit determinism contract for `commit_meta` side-channel emission.
- `AtomicBitSet` emit-once gating solves duplication, but does not guarantee stable output order under parallel workers.
- Require either:
  1) buffered + sorted `commit_meta` flush (e.g., by `commit_id`), or
  2) documented non-deterministic stream order with deterministic key semantics for downstream joins.
- Include acceptance test for no duplicates + expected ordering semantics.

title: Git attribution: lazy author/committer identity enrichment with string interning
description:
## Context
Commit graph does not carry author/committer names/emails. Emitting identity fields requires commit object parsing, which can be expensive if done eagerly for all commits.

Need a lazy strategy:
- Parse commit objects only for commit IDs that actually appear in findings.
- Preserve hot-path characteristics of scanner.

## Goal
Add lazy identity enrichment (author/committer name/email) with minimal memory and CPU overhead.

## Scope
- Extend commit metadata pipeline to support optional identity enrichment.
- Parse commit objects on demand for “referenced by finding” commits only.
- Intern strings into pooled storage and emit dictionary refs (`u32` IDs) instead of repeating full strings.

## Performance Constraints
- Zero impact when identity enrichment is disabled.
- Bounded overhead when enabled:
  - Parse only referenced commits.
  - Cache parsed commit identities to avoid repeat decode.
  - No per-finding string clone.
- Use compact interning strategy (byte arena + index table) to reduce alloc pressure.

## Data-Structure/Algorithm Notes
- Candidate design: intern pool with
  - `Vec<u8>` byte arena
  - `(offset,len)` entries
  - hash map for dedupe to stable `u32` intern IDs
- Metadata emission should expose intern IDs + optional dictionary section to support downstream resolution.

## Correctness Notes
- Handle malformed commit headers robustly (invalid UTF-8, missing fields, odd signatures).
- Ensure author/committer field parsing obeys git object format semantics and remains format-agnostic (sha1/sha256 repos).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Identity data emitted only for commits referenced by findings.
- Repeated identities are interned and not duplicated in output payload.
- Fallback behavior defined for parse failures (no panic; partial metadata allowed).
- Benchmark includes CPU + memory deltas with enrichment off/on.
notes:
Research refinement (decision gate):
- Treat identity strategy as an A/B benchmarked choice, not a fixed design.
- Reason specific to scanner-rs: commit objects are already parsed during commit-graph acquisition path (`artifact_acquire -> commit_loader -> parse_commit`), so eager extraction may be cheaper than assumed.
- Required benchmark comparison:
  1) eager identity extraction+interning during commit load
  2) lazy ODB re-parse for finding-referenced commits only
- Decide based on measured CPU/memory on representative repos; record winner and rationale in issue notes.
close_reason: Completed: lazy author/committer identity enrichment implemented with string interning

title: Git attribution: add deterministic mode alongside fast streaming mode
description:
## Context
Parallel ODB introduction currently allows race-winner attribution context, so commit attribution can vary run-to-run even if finding set is identical.

Relevant note: `src/git_scan/blob_introducer.rs` explicitly documents non-deterministic attribution context in parallel mode.

## Goal
Preserve current fast path while providing explicit deterministic attribution mode for users who require reproducible attribution.

## Scope
- Define two modes:
  - `fast`: streaming attribution, potential context variance in parallel mode.
  - `deterministic`: canonicalize per-blob attribution context before final emission.
- Canonicalization order should mirror existing deterministic tie-break strategy principles (similar to finalize canonical context ordering in `src/git_scan/finalize.rs`).
- Document determinism contract clearly in CLI/help/docs.

## Performance Constraints
- `fast` mode remains default and unchanged in throughput behavior.
- `deterministic` mode can cost more, but overhead must be characterized and bounded.
- Avoid global synchronization in fast mode.

## Data-Structure/Algorithm Notes
- Reuse existing canonical compare keys (`commit_id`, path bytes, parent_idx, change_kind, flags) where possible.
- Prefer per-blob context canonicalization after dedupe boundaries rather than introducing extra contention in worker loops.

## Correctness Notes
- Deterministic mode must be reproducible across repeated runs with same input/config and thread count.
- Define behavior across differing thread counts (either guaranteed or explicitly documented as out-of-contract).

## Acceptance Criteria
- New mode flag/config accepted and tested.
- Repeated-run determinism tests added (parallel scans, same repo/config).
- Fast vs deterministic perf comparison documented with throughput and attribution-stability metrics.
notes:
Research refinement (determinism scope):

title: Move per-task skipped vec into SchedulerPackScratch
description:
In runner_exec.rs lines 1307 and 1392, each call to run_scheduler_pack_task creates a new `let mut skipped = Vec::new()` to collect SkippedCandidate records. This allocates a fresh Vec on every task execution (per-plan or per-shard). The project uses SchedulerPackScratch (line 1012) specifically to avoid per-task allocations — cache and exec_scratch are already reused across tasks via this pattern.

Fix: Add a `skipped: Vec<SkippedCandidate>` field to SchedulerPackScratch. In run_scheduler_pack_task, instead of `let mut skipped = Vec::new()`, do `scratch.skipped.clear()` and pass `&mut scratch.skipped` to collect_skipped_candidates. Then use std::mem::take to move the populated vec into SchedulerPackExecOutput (the output takes ownership, scratch gets an empty vec back). On the next task, prepare/clear will work on the empty vec, and after the first task the take'd vec gets replaced — so we need to handle the capacity loss.

Better approach: swap the vec out of scratch into the output, and swap the output's previous empty vec back. But since SchedulerPackExecOutput is newly constructed, just use std::mem::take and accept that the scratch vec loses capacity after the first task. The key win is that the very first task for each worker still allocates (unavoidable), but subsequent tasks on the same worker reuse capacity as long as we structure it correctly.

Cleanest approach: 
1. Add `skipped: Vec<SkippedCandidate>` to SchedulerPackScratch
2. At task start: scratch.skipped.clear()  
3. Call collect_skipped_candidates(plan, &report.skips, &mut scratch.skipped)
4. Build output with: skipped: std::mem::take(&mut scratch.skipped)
5. The take leaves an empty vec (0 capacity) in scratch, but next task's collect_skipped_candidates will grow it once and subsequent tasks with similar skip counts reuse that capacity

title: Replace BFS exec_order with cache-aware DFS subtree-contiguous ordering
description:
## Problem

`build_exec_order` in `src/git_scan/pack_plan.rs:624` uses Kahn's algorithm with
a BTreeSet ready queue, producing BFS-like topological ordering. This maximizes
cache frontier width: all roots are processed before any depth-1 node, forcing
all base objects to survive simultaneously in PackCache until dependents arrive.

When a base is evicted before its last dependent, `decode_base_from_pack` must
re-walk the entire delta chain (re-parse headers, re-inflate, re-apply deltas).
This fallback is tracked by `base_cache_misses` and `fallback_base_decodes`.

## Research

### Git C (index-pack.c) — battle-tested approach
Uses LIFO work stack with `children_remaining` counter per base. Processes
base then ALL its children recursively before next base. Prunes cache when
counter hits zero. This is DFS subtree-contiguous ordering.

### Pebbling game theory (Blocki & Zhou 2016)
The "given a DAG, find processing order minimizing peak cached entries" problem
is the black pebbling game. NP-hard for general DAGs, but for TREES (which
delta chains predominantly are — each delta has exactly one base), postorder
DFS is provably optimal for minimizing peak pebble count.

### Elimination tree ordering (sparse matrix literature)
Postorder traversal of dependency tree minimizes cache working set. Used in
sparse Cholesky factorization — structurally identical to delta chain resolution.

### Graph reordering (Coleman et al.)
Grouping commonly-accessed nodes together yields up to 40% query time improvement.

## Solution

Replace BFS with DFS subtree-contiguous ordering in `build_exec_order`.
Four O(V+E) phases:

1. **Adjacency**: Build edges (base→dependents), indegree. Trigger on ANY delta
   deps (not just forward deps) — backward deps also benefit from contiguity.

2. **Descendant counts**: Reverse BFS from leaves, propagate desc_count upward.
   Exact for trees; over-counts for DAGs (acceptable tie-break heuristic).

3. **DFS with LIFO stack**: Sort children by ascending desc_count (thin subtrees
   first — they complete quickly, aging under CLOCK). Push roots sorted by
   descending desc_count. Push children only when dag_remaining hits zero
   (preserves topo invariant for DAGs).

4. **Validation**: Cycle check. Return None if result matches natural [0..n].

### Why thin-subtrees-first
Thin chains complete quickly and their cache entries age under CLOCK, becoming
evictable before the large subtree starts. Gives the large subtree effectively
more cache capacity.

### Why trigger on all deps (not just forward)
Consider offsets [10, 20, 50] where 20 and 50 both depend on base 10.
Natural ascending: 10, 20, 50 — base 10 survives 2 intervening offsets.
DFS contiguous: 10, 20, 50 — immediate reuse, 0 intervening offsets.
Improvement compounds with interleaved independent chains.

## Files to modify

- `src/git_scan/pack_plan.rs` — rewrite `build_exec_order` (lines 624-697), add unit tests
- `src/git_scan/pack_plan_model.rs` — add `delta_tree_roots` and `delta_tree_max_depth` to PackPlanStats

Files that should NOT change: pack_exec.rs, pack_cache.rs, runner_exec.rs.
The executor already consumes exec_order: Option<Vec<u32>> generically.

## Unit tests to add

- dfs_groups_subtrees_contiguously: Fan-out tree, verify contiguous subtrees
- dfs_thin_subtree_first: Verify thin child processed before fat child
- dfs_linear_chain: 10→20→30→40, verify sequential output
- dfs_dag_shared_base: Node with two parents, verify valid topo order
- dfs_returns_none_no_deps: No delta deps → None
- dfs_returns_none_natural_order: Result matches [0..n] → None
- dfs_cycle_detected: Verify cycle detection error

## Verification

1. cargo test -p scanner-rs — all existing + new tests pass
2. cargo test --test integration — pack exec integration tests pass
3. Benchmark: compare base_cache_hits/(hits+misses), fallback_base_decodes,
   fallback_resolve_nanos, and wall time before/after on real repos
notes:
CONSTRAINT: Diagnostic stats (delta_tree_roots, delta_tree_max_depth) must be
populated via perf_stats helpers, which compile to no-ops without the perf-stats
feature flag. Fields exist in struct unconditionally (zeroed by Default), but
mutations use perf_stats::set_u32() gated behind
#[cfg(all(feature = "perf-stats", debug_assertions))].

A set_u32 helper needs to be added to src/perf_stats.rs (currently only has
set_u64 and set_usize).

The DFS algorithm itself is NOT behind a feature flag — it replaces BFS
unconditionally. Only the diagnostic counters are gated.

## Final Validation Results

### Quality Gates — All Pass
- `cargo fmt --all` — clean (no formatting issues)
- `cargo check` — clean (no compiler warnings)
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` — clean (no lint warnings)
- `cargo test` — 1536 unit tests + 13 doc tests passed, 0 failures

### Functional Validation — 59 Offline-Validation Tests

**API layer (6 tests):** `offline_suppresses_on_invalid`, CRC32 boundary/panic tests,
`offline_validation_none_is_valid`, value suppressor tests.

**Validator unit tests (33 tests):** AWS access key (prefix, charset, A3T),
CRC32-base62 (valid/invalid checksum, too-short), GitHub PAT (valid, wrong prefix,
invalid checksum), Grafana (valid/invalid/too-short), Sentry (structure, prefix,
separator, payload chars, signature), hex/base62/base64 decode edge cases.

**Engine integration tests (4 key tests):**

| Test | Scenario | Result |
|------|----------|--------|
| `offline_validation_suppresses_invalid_root_finding` | Invalid CRC token at root | 0 findings (suppressed), `offline_suppressed == 1` |
| `offline_validation_keeps_valid_root_finding` | Valid CRC token at root | 1 finding retained, `offline_suppressed == 0` |
| `offline_validation_mixed_valid_invalid_and_no_gate` | Valid + invalid + no-gate rule | 2 findings (valid CRC + no-gate kept, invalid CRC suppressed) |
| `offline_validation_does_not_suppress_non_root_findings` | Invalid token via Base64 transform | Finding retained (non-root bypasses gate) |

**Rule YAML parsing tests (16 tests):** Parse/roundtrip for all 5 validator types,
missing-field rejection, unknown-type rejection.

### Performance — No Regression

**Per-validator microbenchmarks (bench/offline_validation):**

| Validator | Case | Latency | Throughput | vs Baseline |
|-----------|------|---------|------------|-------------|
| AWS | valid_akia | 17.6 ns | 1.06 GiB/s | +3% (noise) |
| AWS | valid_a3t | 18.0 ns | 1.04 GiB/s | within noise |
| AWS | invalid_charset | 2.25 ns | 8.28 GiB/s | within noise |
| AWS | invalid_prefix | 2.35 ns | 7.92 GiB/s | within noise |
| Sentry | valid_small | 49.7 ns | 1.40 GiB/s | within noise |
| Sentry | valid_large | 203 ns | 3.17 GiB/s | -23% (improved) |
| Sentry | invalid_prefix | 189 ns | 3.40 GiB/s | -26% (improved) |
| Sentry | invalid_char | 183 ns | 3.52 GiB/s | -31% (improved) |
| Sentry | oversized | 30.1 ns | 28.1 GiB/s | -6% (improved) |

Invalid tokens rejected in 2-30 ns (fast-path early exit). No regressions.

**Full-engine throughput (bench/scanner_throughput):**

| Workload | Throughput |
|----------|-----------|
| tier1 ceiling (random 4MB) | 9.18 GiB/s |
| tier1 ceiling (ascii 4MB) | 28.14 GiB/s |
| full_engine/random_bytes | 130 MiB/s |
| full_engine/clean_ascii | 388 MiB/s |
| full_engine/sparse_anchors | 384 MiB/s |
| full_engine/moderate_secrets | 390 MiB/s |
| full_engine/mixed_realistic | 1.25 GiB/s |

The `post_scan_filter` offline gate has zero overhead when the gate pool is empty
(early-exit on `self.offline_gates.is_empty()`). When gates are active, cost is
bounded to O(findings × per-validator-cost), which is sub-microsecond for typical
workloads.

### Edge-Case Risks & Follow-Ups
- Transform-derived (non-root) findings intentionally bypass offline validation
  because extracted spans are in transformed space, not root space. This is correct
  behavior but means base64-encoded invalid tokens will not be suppressed.
- The current gate set covers 5 validators (AWS, CRC32-base62, GitHub PAT, Grafana,

- No rules currently produce `Indeterminate` verdicts; all validators are

title: Extract sliding-window read loop helper for archive scanning
description:
The code review identified that the sliding-window read loop pattern is triplicated across the three archive format handlers in src/archive/scan.rs. Each format (gzip, tar, zip) has its own copy of the overlap-carry + read-fill + sink-deliver loop.

**Locations:**
- Gzip scan loop: src/archive/scan.rs (search for the gzip arm in scan_archive_impl)
- Tar scan loop: src/archive/scan.rs (tar arm)
- Zip scan loop: src/archive/scan.rs (zip arm)

The loops share the same structure:
1. Carry overlap bytes from end of previous chunk to start of buffer
2. Read new data into remaining buffer space via format-specific reader
3. Deliver chunk to sink via on_entry_chunk
4. Charge budget
5. Loop until EOF or budget hit

**Considerations:**
- The review noted this duplication may be intentional ('strategic') since each format has slightly different reader types and error handling
- A generic helper parameterized over the reader type (or using the TarRead trait) could unify the loop body
- Alternatively, a macro could stamp out the variants
- This is lower priority since the duplication is self-contained within one file and the loops are performance-critical hot paths where abstraction overhead should be zero-cost

**Approach:** Evaluate whether a generic `fn sliding_window_loop<R: Read>(...)` can cleanly abstract over all three without hurting readability or adding trait-object overhead. If the abstraction is awkward, close this as wontfix.

title: Change PackExecError::Spill(String) to Spill(std::io::Error)
description:
In pack_exec.rs lines 1755 and 1775, PackExecError::Spill(String) forces a .to_string() heap allocation when a spill-file I/O operation fails. While this is an error-only path (and the alloc guard assertion runs on the success path so it won't catch this at runtime), it still performs an unnecessary heap allocation during the scan phase. The project philosophy is zero allocation after startup — even error paths should avoid allocating when possible.

Fix: Change the Spill variant from Spill(String) to Spill(std::io::Error). std::io::Error already exists from the OS layer — we just pass ownership instead of converting to String. This eliminates the .to_string() allocation entirely. PackExecError does not derive Clone, so std::io::Error (which is not Clone) is compatible.

Changes required:
1. pack_exec.rs: Change enum variant Spill(String) -> Spill(std::io::Error)
2. pack_exec.rs: Update Display impl for Spill to use write\!(f, "spill error: {err}")
3. pack_exec.rs lines 1755, 1775: Change .map_err(|err| PackExecError::Spill(err.to_string())) to .map_err(PackExecError::Spill)

Only the Spill variant needs changing — the other String-bearing variants (PackRead, Sink, ExternalBase) are constructed in setup/teardown code outside the inner decode loop.

1. RuleCompiled storing large optional gate structs inline (~850+ bytes per rule even when most gates are None)
2. ScratchVec carrying a 16-byte Layout field per instance (11 instances = 440 bytes of metadata overhead)
3. StepArena storing full DecodeStep enums (32 bytes) when hot path only needs StepId (4 bytes)
4. PackedPatterns using Vec (ptr+len+cap) when Box<[T]> (ptr+len) suffices for immutable data
5. ScanScratch mixing hot and cold fields without alignment boundaries

## Design Phases
- **Phase 1 (High-confidence)**: Pool rule gates, shrink ScratchVec, compact StepArena, boxed slices
- **Phase 2 (Aggressive)**: Hot/cold ScanScratch split, lazy allocation, AoS Vectorscan metadata, u32 ScratchVec headers

## Success Criteria
- Lower cycles/byte in tier2/tier3 benchmarks
- Lower L1D miss rate under perf stat
- No semantic regressions (property tests, materialization equivalence)
- Size guard assertions for all refactored types

title: Compact StepArena nodes with deferred DecodeStep materialization
description:
Store a compact StepNode representation in the arena, materialize full DecodeStep only on the cold output path.

## Problem
StepNode stores parent: StepId (4 bytes) + step: DecodeStep (32 bytes) = ~40 bytes per node. But the hot path only uses StepId (4 bytes) — the full DecodeStep data is only needed when materializing findings for output.

## Solution
Replace StepNode with a compact representation:
```rust
#[repr(C)]
pub struct StepNodeCompact {
    parent: u32,          // StepId.0
    kind: u8,             // 0=Transform, 1=Utf16Le, 2=Utf16Be
    _pad: u8,
    transform_idx: u16,   // only for Transform; 0 otherwise
    span_lo: u32,
    span_hi: u32,
}
// Total: 16 bytes (down from ~40)
```

Add materialize() that reconstructs DecodeStep from compact form:
```rust
fn materialize(&self) -> DecodeStep {
    match self.kind {
        0 => DecodeStep::Transform {
            transform_idx: self.transform_idx as usize,
            parent_span: self.span_lo as usize..self.span_hi as usize,
        },
        1 => DecodeStep::Utf16Window {
            endianness: Utf16Endianness::Le,
            parent_span: self.span_lo as usize..self.span_hi as usize,
        },
        2 => DecodeStep::Utf16Window {
            endianness: Utf16Endianness::Be,
            parent_span: self.span_lo as usize..self.span_hi as usize,
        },
        _ => unreachable!(),
    }
}
```

## Correctness constraints
- Ensure transform_idx <= u16::MAX at engine build time (add assertion)
- Ensure spans fit in u32 (already true — the engine uses SpanU32 and EncRef with u32 throughout)
- Add size guard: StepNodeCompact must be exactly 16 bytes
- Unit test: build step chain with transform + utf16, verify materialize() yields identical DecodeSteps

## Impact
- ~60% reduction in arena footprint (40→16 bytes per node)
- Better cache behavior in transform-heavy scans

## Files to modify
- src/engine/decode_state.rs — replace StepNode, update push/materialize
- src/engine/core.rs — update materialization call site (line ~1567-1581)
- src/api.rs — no change needed (DecodeStep enum stays as public API)
close_reason: Compact StepNode from 40 to 16 bytes via CompactDecodeStep

- [ ] When suppressor does not match: finding IS emitted (pass-through)

title: Add --transforms CLI flag for per-transform-type control
description:
## Context

The scanner currently runs URL-percent and Base64 transform decoding on every chunk automatically. This is correct for general-purpose scanning — secrets can be hidden inside encoded layers. However, profiling shows transforms account for the majority of CPU time on the zero-hit path: **533 MiB/s** with transforms vs **4,490 MiB/s** without (8.4x gap). Users scanning known-plaintext corpora (e.g., source code repos with no encoded secrets) pay this cost for zero benefit.

## Goal

Let users selectively disable URL-percent and/or Base64 transform decoding via CLI flags, defaulting to all-enabled (current behavior).

## Scope

**In scope:**

* A `--transforms` CLI flag accepting a comma-separated list: `all` (default), `none`, `url`, `base64`, `url,base64`
* Wire the flag through `FsScanConfig` and `GitSourceConfig` → `build_engine()` → `demo_transforms()` filtering
* When a transform is disabled, its `TransformConfig` is excluded from the transforms vec entirely (not just `TransformMode::Disabled`) — zero overhead
* Log a warning to stderr when transforms are disabled: "Transform decoding disabled — encoded secrets will not be detected"

**Out of scope:**

* Per-rule transform overrides
* Runtime transform switching (mid-scan)
* UTF-16 variant toggling (separate concern, already has `scan_utf16_variants` in `Tuning`)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `--transforms=none` achieves throughput within 10% of the empty-transforms ceiling (~4,490 MiB/s baseline)
- [ ] `--transforms=url` disables only Base64; `--transforms=base64` disables only URL-percent
- [ ] Default behavior (no flag) is identical to current behavior — all transforms enabled
- [ ] All existing tests pass when flag is absent
- [ ] Warning printed to stderr when any transform is disabled

## Technical Direction

* **Approach:** Filter `demo_transforms()` output based on a `TransformPolicy` enum/set before passing to `Engine::new`. No engine-internal changes needed.
* Add `transforms: Option<TransformPolicy>` field to both `FsScanConfig` and `GitSourceConfig`
* `TransformPolicy` can be a simple enum: `All`, `None`, `Only(HashSet<TransformId>)` — or just a pair of bools (`enable_url_percent`, `enable_base64`)
* Wire through `build_engine()` and `run_git()` — both paths already accept transforms as a parameter
* The existing `TransformMode::Disabled` mechanism is unnecessary here since we can just exclude the config entirely from the vec
* **CLI parsing:** `clap` value parser with comma-separated values mapping to the policy

## References

* `src/demo.rs:61-87` — `demo_transforms()` returns the hardcoded transform list
* `src/unified/mod.rs:60-74` — `FsScanConfig` struct
* `src/unified/orchestrator.rs:498-502` — `build_engine()` wiring
* `src/api.rs:75-77` — `TransformId` enum (two variants: `UrlPercent`, `Base64`)
* Performance data: all-transforms=533 MiB/s, no-transforms=4,490 MiB/s, url-gate-only=655 MiB/s

title: Fix VectorscanCounters false sharing with per-worker counters
description:
Address potential false sharing in VectorscanCounters where 11 adjacent AtomicU64 fields can share cache lines.

## Problem
VectorscanCounters in src/engine/core.rs has 11 adjacent AtomicU64 fields (88 bytes) with no explicit alignment. Multiple threads incrementing different atomics can cause false-sharing on the same cache line. While Relaxed ordering mitigates synchronization cost, the cache-line bouncing remains.

## Solution options

### Option A (best): Per-worker counters with merge
```rust
struct VectorscanCountersLocal {
    scans_attempted: u64,
    scans_ok: u64,
    scans_err: u64,
    // ... non-atomic, per-worker
}
// Merge at end of scan batch
```
- Eliminates atomics entirely in hot path
- Follows existing WorkerMetricsLocal pattern

### Option B: Pad each atomic
```rust
struct VectorscanCounters {
    scans_attempted: CachePadded<AtomicU64>,
    // ... each padded to 64 bytes
}
```
- Simple but wastes memory (11 × 64 = 704 bytes vs 88 bytes)

## Recommendation
Option A is preferred — it follows the existing WorkerMetricsLocal pattern and avoids atomics in the hot path entirely.

## Files to modify
- src/engine/core.rs — refactor VectorscanCounters
- Merge logic at scan completion

## Phase 2 — only if stats feature is used during perf benchmarking. If stats is debug-only, deprioritize.
notes: Implemented false-sharing mitigation via cache-line padded atomics: introduced #[repr(align(64))] CachePaddedAtomicU64 and switched VectorscanCounters fields to padded counters. This isolates frequently updated counters to separate cache lines while preserving existing stats API and call sites.
close_reason: Mitigated Vectorscan stats false sharing with cache-line padded counters

title: YAML rules loading with deterministic ordering and VsDbCache reuse
description:
## Context
Today all rules are compiled into the binary via `gitleaks_rules()` in `src/gitleaks_rules.rs`. This makes rule iteration slow (recompile the whole binary) and prevents users from customizing their rule set. The Vectorscan DB disk cache (`VsDbCache`) already handles cache-key-based reuse of compiled `.hsdb` files, and `policy_hash` already canonically encodes rules for git scan caching.

## Goal
Load rules from an external YAML file at startup, replacing the compiled-in rule set, while reusing existing `VsDbCache` and `policy_hash` infrastructure for deterministic caching.

## Scope
**In scope:**
- Add `--rules=<file>` flag to both `scan fs` and `scan git`
- YAML schema mirrors `RuleSpec` fields (name, anchors, radius, regex as pattern string, etc.)
- Parse YAML into `Vec<RuleSpec>` at startup
- Ship a `default_rules.yaml` sibling file (equivalent to today's `gitleaks_rules()`)
- When `--rules` is not specified, load `default_rules.yaml` from next to the binary
- Remove compiled-in `gitleaks_rules()` — all rules are external
- Reuse existing `VsDbCache` (cache keys already derived from patterns/flags/IDs)
- Reuse existing `policy_hash` (already order-invariant for rules)

**Out of scope:**
- Directory scanning / multi-file rules
- Rule merging or overlaying
- Compiled rule packs
- Rule validation beyond what `RuleSpec::assert_valid()` already does
- Hot-reload of rules

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Running the same scan twice with the same YAML rules reuses cached `*.hsdb` files (no recompilation)
- [ ] Changing a YAML rule's regex or anchors produces new cache keys and new `*.hsdb` files
- [ ] Rule ordering is stable across runs (single-file array index)
- [ ] `policy_hash` changes when scanning-relevant rule fields change (because `RuleSpec::encode_policy` includes them)
- [ ] `--rules=<file>` works for both `scan fs` and `scan git`
- [ ] When `--rules` is omitted, `default_rules.yaml` is loaded from the binary's sibling directory
- [ ] Clear error message if the rules file is missing or malformed

## Technical Direction
- **Serde**: Add `serde::Deserialize` to a `YamlRuleSpec` struct with string-typed fields, then convert to `RuleSpec` (compile regex, parse anchors from strings to `&'static [u8]` via leaking or an arena)
- **Anchor encoding**: Anchors as hex strings or UTF-8 strings in YAML, converted to `&'static [u8]` at load time
- **Static lifetime**: Since rules live for the program's duration, `Box::leak` the parsed strings/vecs to produce `&'static` references matching `RuleSpec`'s current lifetime requirements
- **Default file location**: `std::env::current_exe()` → parent dir → join `default_rules.yaml`
- **CLI parsing**: Add `--rules=<path>` to the hand-rolled parser in `src/unified/cli.rs`, threaded into both `FsArgs` and `GitArgs`
- **Existing cache/hash untouched**: `VsDbCache` and `policy_hash` already work generically over `&[RuleSpec]` — no changes needed there

## References
- `src/api.rs:581` — `RuleSpec` definition
- `src/engine/vs_cache.rs` — `VsDbCache` cache key and storage
- `src/git_scan/policy_hash.rs` — `policy_hash()` with order-invariant rule encoding
- `src/unified/cli.rs` — hand-rolled CLI parser
- `src/gitleaks_rules.rs` — current compiled-in rules (to be converted to YAML)
- `src/demo.rs:57` — `demo_rules()` entry point

title: Split ScanScratch into hot/cold regions with alignment boundaries
description:
Separate ScanScratch into hot and cold nested structs with explicit cache-line alignment between them.

## Problem
ScanScratch has 47 fields mixing hot scan-loop fields with cold/conditional fields. Hot metadata (hit_acc_pool, touched_pairs, windows, out) shares cache lines with cold fields (decode_ring, pending wheels, base64_stats) causing unnecessary cache pollution.

## Solution (Approach A — low risk)
```rust
pub struct ScanScratch {
    hot: ScanScratchHot,   // out, work_q, hit_acc_pool, touched_pairs, windows, expanded, spans, seen_findings_scan
    #[repr(align(64))]
    cold: ScanScratchCold, // decode_ring, pending_windows, stream state, base64_stats, entropy_scratch
}
```

This doesn't change ownership or lifetimes — just improves packing and prevents hot/cold cache-line sharing.

## Categorization
**Hot** (scan loop critical):
- out, norm_hash, drop_hint_end, work_q, work_head
- hit_acc_pool, touched_pairs, windows, expanded, spans
- seen_findings_scan, max_findings, findings_dropped

**Cold** (conditional/streaming):
- decode_ring, window_bytes, vs_stream_matches
- pending_spans, span_streams, pending_windows
- tmp_findings, tmp_drop_hint_end, tmp_norm_hash
- entropy_scratch (1284 bytes\!), base64_stats
- slab, seen, seen_findings, root_span_map_ctx
- All VsScratch options

## Files to modify
- src/engine/scratch.rs — restructure into nested structs
- All files that access ScanScratch fields — update field paths (scratch.hot.X / scratch.cold.X)

## Phase 2 — only pursue after Phase 1 benchmarks show remaining cache pressure
notes: Implemented hot/cold ScanScratch layout split with a 64-byte alignment boundary marker and #[repr(C)] field-order guarantee; updated docs/memory-management.md and added layout regression test scanscratch_cold_region_is_cacheline_aligned.

title: Add --event-format=text|json|sarif output styles via new EventSink implementations
description:
## Context
The unified CLI emits structured scan events via the `EventSink` trait (`src/unified/events.rs`), with `JsonlEventSink` as the only format. CI integrations need SARIF for GitHub Code Scanning, JSON for programmatic consumption, and human-readable text for terminal use. The architecture already supports this — `EventFormat` enum, `EventEncoder` trait, and `build_event_sink()` factory are all extension points.

## Goal
Add `--event-format=text|json|sarif` output styles as new `EventSink` implementations, keeping scanning hot paths completely unchanged.

## Scope
**In scope:**
- Extend `EventFormat` enum with `Text`, `Json`, `Sarif` variants
- Implement `TextEventSink` — compact one-liner by default, multi-line with `--verbose`
- Implement `JsonEventSink` — streaming JSON array document
- Implement `SarifEventSink` — SARIF 2.1.0 with byteOffset-based regions
- Factor JSON escaping helpers into a reusable `json_write` module (shared by JSONL/JSON/SARIF)
- Optimize `JsonlEventSink` to use thread-local buffer reuse instead of per-emit `Vec` allocation
- Wire new formats into `parse_event_format()` and `build_event_sink()`

**Out of scope:**
- `--output=<path>` file output (follow-up story)
- Fingerprints, grouping/dedup across files/commits
- Line/column/snippet enrichment
- Web UI viewer

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `scanner-rs scan fs --path <dir> --event-format=text` prints one-liner findings to stdout
- [ ] `--event-format=text --verbose` prints multi-line finding blocks
- [ ] `--event-format=json` outputs valid JSON array parseable by `serde_json::from_slice`
- [ ] `--event-format=sarif` outputs valid SARIF 2.1.0 JSON with required envelope keys (`version`, `$schema`, `runs`) and one result per finding
- [ ] No interleaving/corruption under multi-threaded emission (unit test: spawn N threads, emit M events, validate output)
- [ ] Existing `--event-format=jsonl` output unchanged (default)
- [ ] JSONL per-emit allocation reduced via thread-local buffer reuse

## Technical Direction
- **Pattern**: Mirror `JsonlEventSink` structure — `Mutex<BufWriter<W>>`, format outside lock, `write_all()` inside lock
- **JSON sink**: Write `[` on construction, `,\n` between results (track `first: AtomicBool`), `]` on `flush()`
- **SARIF sink**: Same streaming pattern as JSON sink but emit SARIF envelope. On `flush()`, close the `results` array and `runs`/root braces
- **Text sink compact**: `{path}:{start}-{end}  {rule_name}  ({source})` — one line per finding, summary/progress events as-is
- **Text sink verbose**: Multi-line block with labeled fields (rule, path, range, source, commit if present)
- **JSON escaping module**: Extract `write_json_str`, `write_json_bytes`, `write_u64`, `write_f64` from `JsonlEncoder` into `src/unified/json_write.rs`. All sinks import from there.
- **Thread-local buffer**: Use `std::cell::RefCell<Vec<u8>>` in a `thread_local!` macro for `JsonlEventSink::emit()` to reuse allocation across calls
- **SARIF result mapping**: `ruleId` = `rule_name`, `message.text` = `"Secret matched rule {rule_name}"`, `locations[0].physicalLocation.artifactLocation.uri` = escaped path, `region.byteOffset` = start, `region.byteLength` = end - start

## References
- `src/unified/events.rs` — EventSink trait, JsonlEventSink, JsonlEncoder
- `src/unified/mod.rs:102-108` — EventFormat enum
- `src/unified/cli.rs:342-350` — parse_event_format()
- `src/unified/orchestrator.rs:229-234` — build_event_sink()
- [SARIF 2.1.0 spec](https://docs.oasis-open.org/sarif/sarif/v2.1.0/sarif-v2.1.0.html)

title: Optimize JsonlEventSink with thread-local buffer reuse
description:
## Context
`JsonlEventSink::emit()` currently allocates a new `Vec::with_capacity(256)` per event. Under high-throughput scanning this creates unnecessary allocation churn. Thread-local buffer reuse eliminates this.

## Goal
Replace per-emit `Vec` allocation with a thread-local reusable buffer in `JsonlEventSink`.

## Deliverables

- Clear buffer between uses (preserves capacity)
- Mutex still held only for `write_all()`, not formatting

- `BUF.with(|cell| { let mut buf = cell.borrow_mut(); buf.clear(); ... })` pattern
- Fallback: if `borrow_mut` fails (reentrant call), fall back to fresh `Vec` — shouldn't happen but be defensive

title: Git attribution: emit deduped commit_meta dictionary keyed by commit_id
description:
## Context
After wiring `commit_id` into finding events, repeating commit metadata on every finding wastes bytes and CPU (OID hex formatting, repeated serialization). `scanner-rs` already has O(1) commit metadata lookup via `CommitGraphIndex`.

Relevant primitives:
- `CommitGraphIndex::commit_oid()` and `CommitGraphIndex::committer_timestamp()` (`src/git_scan/commit_graph.rs`).
- Existing finding event already carries `commit_id` (`src/unified/events.rs`).
- Existing lock-free dedupe primitive: `AtomicBitSet` (`src/stdx/atomic_bitset.rs`).

## Goal
Add a deduped commit metadata side channel/table keyed by `commit_id` so findings stay compact while still exposing commit OID/time.

## Scope
- Introduce a `commit_meta` event/table emitted once per commit ID encountered in findings.
- Include at least:
  - `commit_id` (u32 graph position)
  - `commit_oid` (raw bytes or canonical hex representation)
  - `committer_timestamp` (u64 epoch seconds)
- Keep finding events compact (do not duplicate OID/time per finding).

## Performance Constraints
- Emit-once guarantee under concurrency using atomic bitset gating.
- O(1) lookup from commit_id -> metadata via precomputed arrays.
- Avoid per-finding OID formatting and repeated allocation.
- Keep serialization in manual writer path; avoid introducing dynamic JSON alloc churn in hot loop.
- Target regression: statistically insignificant at repo-scale (<1-2%), with p50/p95 checks.

## Data-Structure/Algorithm Notes
- Dense membership: atomic bitset sized to `CommitGraphIndex::len()`.
- Metadata storage: SoA-leaning representation for cache locality (packed OIDs + timestamp vecs; avoid scattered heap objects).
- Sink path should accept dictionary-style metadata emission for downstream join by `commit_id`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every commit ID appearing in findings has exactly one matching `commit_meta` emission.
- No duplicate `commit_meta` under parallel scanning.
- Findings remain compact and reference commit metadata by ID.
- JSONL/text/sarif behavior documented for new metadata channel.
- Perf evidence included: before/after throughput and output size deltas.
notes:
Research refinement (implementation-critical):
- Add explicit determinism contract for `commit_meta` side-channel emission.
- `AtomicBitSet` emit-once gating solves duplication, but does not guarantee stable output order under parallel workers.
- Require either:
  1) buffered + sorted `commit_meta` flush (e.g., by `commit_id`), or
  2) documented non-deterministic stream order with deterministic key semantics for downstream joins.
- Include acceptance test for no duplicates + expected ordering semantics.

title: ScratchVec: use u32 for len/cap fields
description:
Optional aggressive variant: store len and cap as u32 internally in ScratchVec, indexing with usize externally.

## Problem
After removing Layout, ScratchVec is (ptr, len, cap) = 24 bytes. With u32 len/cap it would be (ptr, len, cap) = 16 bytes — saving another 8 bytes per instance (11 instances = 88 bytes).

## Solution
```rust
pub struct ScratchVec<T> {
    ptr: NonNull<MaybeUninit<T>>,
    len: u32,
    cap: u32,
}
```

External API still uses usize:
```rust
pub fn len(&self) -> usize { self.len as usize }
pub fn capacity(&self) -> usize { self.cap as usize }
```

## Invariant
- Capacity must always be ≤ u32::MAX
- This is likely true given existing u32 span/offset design throughout the engine
- Add debug_assert!(cap <= u32::MAX) in with_capacity/grow

## Tradeoff
- Limits max elements to ~4 billion (sufficient for scanner workloads)
- Adds u32↔usize conversion in API boundary
- Requires explicit invariant documentation

## Files to modify
- src/scratch_memory.rs

## Phase 2 aggressive variant — only if profiling shows ScratchVec header size is still a bottleneck
notes: Converted ScratchVec internal len/cap storage to u32 while preserving usize external API. Added capacity guard in with_capacity for cap > u32::MAX, updated all internal pointer/index arithmetic through usize conversion boundaries, and updated size guard (16 bytes on 64-bit).

title: Split Engine rules into hot/cold arrays
description:
Separate Engine rule storage into hot (scan-loop) and cold (reporting/debug) arrays for better cache packing.

## Problem
After pooling gates, the remaining RuleHot struct may still include fields only needed at reporting time (e.g., name: &'static str). If the hot array is iterated densely, cold fields waste cache bandwidth.

## Solution
```rust
pub struct Engine {
    rules_hot: Vec<RuleHot>,   // scan-critical: flags, indices, must_contain, re
    rules_cold: Vec<RuleCold>, // reporting: name, metadata
}
```

Access pattern:
- Hot path uses rules_hot[rule_id] for gate checks and regex
- Cold path (finding emission) uses rules_cold[rule_id] for name

## Tradeoff
- Slight code complexity: two arrays indexed in parallel
- Only worthwhile if Phase 1 benchmarks show rules_hot is still too large for dense iteration

- src/engine/buffer_scan.rs — use rules_hot
- src/engine/window_validate.rs — use rules_hot, rules_cold for findings

title: Reorder RuleHot fields for cache-line packing
description:
After the pool refactor, reorder RuleHot fields so frequently touched values are in the first cache line.

## Problem
Even after pooling gates out of RuleCompiled, field ordering matters. The hot path checks flags and simple gates before doing expensive work. If hot fields are scattered across cache lines, we waste bandwidth.

## Solution
Order fields by access frequency in the hot path (run_rule_on_window / scan_rules_on_buffer):

First cache line (64 bytes) — touched on every window:
1. needs_assignment_shape_check: bool
2. secret_group: Option<u16>
3. must_contain: Option<&'static [u8]>
4. confirm_all_idx: Option<NonZeroU32>
5. keywords_idx: Option<NonZeroU32>
6. two_phase_idx: Option<NonZeroU32>
7. entropy parameters (if kept inline — EntropyCompiled is only ~20 bytes)
8. local_context_idx: Option<NonZeroU32>

Second cache line — touched only on regex match:
9. re: Regex
10. name: &'static str

## Depends on
- Pool optional gates out of RuleCompiled (scratch-scanner-rs-83m)

## Notes

- Verify with std::mem::offset_of! assertions in tests

title: [Epic] Persistence MVP for deterministic FS findings

## Context
The scanner currently emits findings as streaming events with intentionally non-deterministic cross-worker ordering (`src/unified/events.rs`) and without persistence-grade identity fields. ## Goal

## Scope
**In scope:**
- Stable identity derivation independent of worker ordering, batching, and chunk boundaries.

- Append-only segment writer with bounded backpressure and crash-safe finalize.

- Mirror atomic persistence principles from git finalize/persist flow (`src/git_scan/persist.rs`, `src/git_scan/finalize.rs`).

title: Convert PackedPatterns from Vec to Box<[T]>
description:
Replace Vec<u8> and Vec<u32> in PackedPatterns with Box<[u8]> and Box<[u32]> since these are immutable after compilation.

## Problem
PackedPatterns stores `bytes: Vec<u8>` and `offsets: Vec<u32>`. Vec carries (ptr, len, cap) = 24 bytes per field. After rule compilation, these are never mutated — the capacity field is wasted metadata.

## Solution
```rust
pub(super) struct PackedPatterns {
    pub(super) bytes: Box<[u8]>,    // (ptr, len) = 16 bytes
    pub(super) offsets: Box<[u32]>, // (ptr, len) = 16 bytes
}
```

Build with Vecs during compilation, then finalize:
```rust
let bytes: Box<[u8]> = bytes_vec.into_boxed_slice();
let offsets: Box<[u32]> = offsets_vec.into_boxed_slice();
```

## Impact
- Saves 16 bytes per PackedPatterns instance (48→32 bytes)
- Each gate struct has [PackedPatterns; 3], saving 48 bytes per gate
- ConfirmAllCompiled: 240→192 bytes
- KeywordsCompiled: 144→96 bytes
- TwoPhaseCompiled: 160→112 bytes
- Also trims heap: no spare capacity slop

## Files to modify
- src/engine/rule_repr.rs — change field types, update construction code
- Any builder/compilation code that constructs PackedPatterns

## Tradeoff
- Slight refactor of construction code (builder → finalize pattern)
- No runtime cost in scanning; purely compile-time cost
- Better determinism (no spare capacity variation)
close_reason: Converted PackedPatterns Vec to Box<[T]>, saves 8 bytes per field

title: P0: Bound .git/shallow ingestion to prevent pre-traversal memory exhaustion
description:
## Summary
`src/git_scan/commit_loader.rs::load_shallow_boundary_roots` currently reads every non-empty line from `.git/shallow` into a `HashSet<OidBytes>` with no byte or count guard.

That means a repository with an abnormally large (or maliciously bloated) shallow file can force memory growth before `max_commits` and other commit traversal limits are enforced.

## Scope
This follow-up is specifically about **bounded shallow-root ingestion**. The shallow-boundary correctness fix is already landed; this issue addresses memory safety and failure mode hardening.

## Impact
- Potential OOM or severe memory pressure in artifact acquisition (`scan git`) on hostile or pathological repos.
- Failure happens before commit traversal limits (`max_commits`) are useful.
- This is reachable in production scans because `.git/shallow` is repository-controlled input.

## Current Behavior (Code Pointers)
- `load_shallow_boundary_roots` opens `<gitdir>/shallow` and `<commondir>/shallow` and inserts each valid OID into an unbounded `HashSet`.
- Callers: `acquire_commit_graph` and `acquire_commit_graph_with_identities` in `src/git_scan/artifact_acquire.rs`.

## Literature / Reference Implementations
The relevant real-world behavior to anchor against:

1. Git shallow file format and semantics:
   - <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/git/git/master/Documentation/technical/shallow.adoc>
   - <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/git/git/master/Documentation/gitrepository-layout.adoc>
2. Git's own shallow handling implementation (`shallow.c`):
   - <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/git/git/master/shallow.c>
3. libgit2 shallow/grafts handling:
   - <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/libgit2/libgit2/main/src/libgit2/grafts.c>
4. JGit object directory/shallow plumbing:
   - <https://github.com/eclipse-jgit/jgit/blob/master/org.eclipse.jgit/src/org/eclipse/jgit/internal/storage/file/ObjectDirectory.java>
5. Dulwich repository shallow handling:
   - <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jelmer/dulwich/master/dulwich/repo.py>
6. gitoxide shallow support crate:
   - <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GitoxideLabs/gitoxide/main/gix-shallow/src/lib.rs>

Observation to preserve in implementation notes: common Git ecosystems parse shallow roots but generally leave resource policy to callers; our scanner needs explicit ingestion bounds because it scans untrusted repositories at scale.

## Proposed Design Direction
1. Add explicit shallow-ingestion limits to commit-load policy (no CLI changes in this issue):
   - `max_shallow_file_bytes` (per-file byte cap)
   - `max_shallow_roots` (max unique shallow OIDs accepted)
2. Apply an effective root limit:
   - `effective_max_roots = min(max_shallow_roots, max_commits)`
   - Rationale: cannot traverse more than `max_commits` commit nodes anyway.
3. Fail fast with explicit errors when limits are exceeded:
   - Oversized shallow file
   - Too many shallow roots
4. Keep existing behavior for:
   - Missing shallow files => empty set
   - Invalid OID lines => invalid-data error
5. Do not change CLI surface in this task; wire via existing internal limit structs/defaults.

## Implementation Notes To Capture In PR
- Bound checking must happen during ingestion, not after full set construction.
- Avoid hidden silent truncation; prefer explicit error so operators can diagnose.
- Ensure linked-worktree case (`git_dir` + `common_dir`) still works with per-file checks.
- Error messages should include path and configured/effective limit values.

## Test Matrix (must be implemented)
1. `no_shallow_file_returns_empty_set`
   - Missing shallow files in both locations returns empty set.
2. `invalid_shallow_oid_reports_invalid_data`
   - Existing invalid line behavior remains unchanged.
3. `oversized_shallow_file_fails_fast`
   - File size above cap returns explicit limit error.
4. `too_many_shallow_roots_fails_fast`
   - More than effective root limit returns explicit limit error.
5. `duplicates_do_not_bypass_limit`
   - Duplicates should not inflate unique count; verify counting semantics explicitly.
6. `effective_limit_respects_max_commits`
   - `max_shallow_roots > max_commits` still clamps at `max_commits`.
7. `linked_worktree_common_dir_shallow_respects_limits`
   - Both shallow file locations processed with bounds.
8. Integration regression guard
   - Existing shallow-boundary success test remains green under default limits.
9. Simulation/test-suite gap closure
   - Add/extend simulation or integration fixture coverage so this condition is caught by automated suites.

## Why This Escaped Existing Tests
- Existing regression focused on missing parent semantics at shallow boundary, not ingestion resource caps.
- No test currently synthesizes abnormally large shallow files or root counts.
- Simulation coverage does not model shallow-file resource exhaustion behavior.

## Done Criteria
- Limit fields added and validated in internal configuration defaults.
- Ingestion loop is bounded and fails fast with typed errors.
- Test matrix above implemented (or any deviations documented in issue notes).
- `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` passes.

title: Pool optional gates out of RuleCompiled into Engine-owned storage
description:
Move large optional gate structs out of RuleCompiled into engine-owned pools, replacing inline Option<T> with compact Option<NonZeroU32> indices.

## Problem
RuleCompiled is ~850+ bytes per rule because it stores ConfirmAllCompiled (~240B), KeywordsCompiled (~144B), TwoPhaseCompiled (~160B), and LocalContextSpec inline as Option<T>. Even when a gate is None, the full size of T is reserved in memory. This bloats the working set for scan_rules_on_buffer / run_rule_on_window.

## Solution
Replace inline Option<T> with compact pool indices:
```rust
// In RuleCompiled (renamed to RuleHot):
confirm_all_idx: Option<NonZeroU32>,   // 4 bytes vs ~256 bytes
keywords_idx: Option<NonZeroU32>,      // 4 bytes vs ~160 bytes
two_phase_idx: Option<NonZeroU32>,     // 4 bytes vs ~176 bytes
local_context_idx: Option<NonZeroU32>, // 4 bytes vs variable
```

Engine owns the actual storage:
```rust
pub struct Engine {
    rules: Vec<RuleHot>,
    confirm_all_pool: Vec<ConfirmAllCompiled>,
    keywords_pool: Vec<KeywordsCompiled>,
    two_phase_pool: Vec<TwoPhaseCompiled>,
    local_context_pool: Vec<LocalContextSpec>,
}
```

## Files to modify
- src/engine/rule_repr.rs — refactor RuleCompiled struct, add pool index fields
- src/engine/core.rs — add pool Vecs to Engine, populate during rule compilation
- src/engine/buffer_scan.rs — pass engine ref for pool lookups in scan_rules_on_buffer
- src/engine/window_validate.rs — pass engine ref for pool lookups in run_rule_on_window
- src/engine/vectorscan_prefilter.rs — update any direct rule field accesses

## Tradeoffs
- One extra dependent load when a gate exists (pool[idx] access)
- Typically cheaper than dragging hundreds of unused bytes into cache for every rule

## Correctness
- Unit test: for each rule, if confirm_all_idx.is_some() then pool entry matches original behavior
- Property test: pooled vs inline outputs identical for random windows
- Add size guard: RuleHot must be ≤ 96 bytes (down from ~850+)

## This is the single highest-ROI optimization in the analysis.

title: Git scan fails on shallow clone boundary with CommitNotFound
description:
## Summary
`scan git` fails during artifact acquisition on shallow clones (repro: VS Code clone) when commit loading traverses to a parent OID that is intentionally absent beyond the shallow boundary.

## Reproduction
```bash
/usr/bin/time target/release/scanner-rs scan git --repo="../vscode" --null-sink
```
Observed error:
```
git scan failed: artifact acquisition failed: commit loading failed: commit f8bd1cfbc94b253e95852185b71646f4ea42770f not found in MIDX packs or loose objects
```

## Investigation Findings
- `../vscode` is a shallow repository (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` => `true`).
- `.git/shallow` contains commit `490c747f076792a456ea4bb4ea356bbefca3d3bb`.
- That shallow commit’s object header includes parent `f8bd1cfbc94b253e95852185b71646f4ea42770f`, which is not locally present (verified via `git cat-file`).
- Current loader behavior in `src/git_scan/commit_loader.rs` always enqueues all parsed parents and treats missing parents as fatal `CommitNotFound`.
- This conflicts with shallow-boundary semantics where parents beyond shallow roots are expected to be unavailable.

## Why Existing Tests Missed This
- Current integration fixtures create full local repos and do not create shallow clones.
- Git simulation coverage currently models packed/loose behaviors but not shallow-boundary parent elision semantics.
- A related missing-object integration test (`missing_loose_object_yields_partial`) was removed earlier, leaving this path uncovered.

## Required First Step (before fix)
Add a regression integration test that creates a depth-1 shallow clone and reproduces the current `CommitNotFound` artifact-acquire failure.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Add regression test reproducing shallow-boundary failure deterministically.
2. Update commit loading/artifact acquisition to honor shallow boundaries (treat beyond-boundary parents as external roots, not fatal missing objects).
3. Verify `scan git` succeeds on shallow clones (including the VS Code reproduction case).
4. Confirm no regression for full clones and existing loose-object fallback scenarios.
notes:
Investigation confirms this is a shallow-boundary traversal bug. In ../vscode, .git/shallow contains 490c747f076792a456ea4bb4ea356bbefca3d3bb; raw commit headers for that OID include parent f8bd1cfbc94b253e95852185b71646f4ea42770f, which is absent from local ODB. Added regression reproducer at tests/integration/git_scan_validation.rs:535 (shallow_clone_boundary_reproduces_commit_not_found_during_artifact_acquire). Test constructs a depth-1 file:// clone, verifies boundary parent is absent via git cat-file -e, and asserts current scanner failure is ArtifactAcquire -> CommitLoad -> CommitNotFound for that parent.
Implemented shallow-boundary handling in commit loading. commit_loader now reads shallow roots from <gitdir>/shallow (and <commondir>/shallow for linked worktrees) via load_shallow_boundary_roots; BFS traversal treats those commits as boundary roots and does not enqueue their parents. Wired through artifact acquisition for both commit graph paths (with and without identity enrichment). Updated regression to assert success on depth-1 shallow clone: shallow_clone_boundary_treats_missing_parent_as_external_root. Verified with: cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features; targeted integration tests for shallow + prior loose/packed scenarios; and /usr/bin/time target/release/scanner-rs scan git --repo=../vscode --null-sink now completes successfully.

title: [Epic] Value-level suppressors on extracted secret bytes
description:
## Context

The secret scanner currently has no mechanism to suppress findings based on the extracted secret value itself. This means well-known placeholder tokens (e.g., `AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE`), documentation examples, and dummy credentials generate false positives that waste analyst time.

## Goal

Add a first-class, YAML-driven, per-rule `value_suppressors_any` field that suppresses findings when the extracted secret bytes contain any of the configured literal patterns. This leverages the existing `PackedPatterns` + `contains_any_memmem` infrastructure for zero-allocation, post-match suppression.

## Design Principles

- **YAML-native**: Suppressors are declared per-rule in the rules YAML file, not in Rust overlays.
- **Post-match only**: Evaluated after regex match + entropy pass + secret extraction. No-hit path is unchanged.
- **Secret-bytes scoped**: Suppression checks the extracted secret slice, not the full match or context line. This is less risky than line-level stopwords.
- **Existing infrastructure**: Reuses `PackedPatterns`, `PackedPatternsBuilder`, `contains_any_memmem`, gate pool indexing pattern on `Engine`/`RuleCompiled`.

## Architecture

Pipeline insertion point in `window_validate.rs`:

1. Regex capture match (existing)
2. Entropy check (existing)
3. Extract secret span (existing)
4. **Value suppressor gate on `secret_bytes` (NEW)**
5. Local context gate (existing)
6. Hash + emit (existing)

Compilation: `value_suppressors_any` strings → interned `&'static [&'static [u8]]` → `PackedPatterns` (raw only, no UTF-16 expansion needed) → pooled on `Engine` → index stored on `RuleCompiled`.

## Out of Scope (follow-ups if telemetry warrants)

- Case-insensitive matching (`value_suppressors_ci`)
- Exact-match variant (`value_suppressors_exact_any`)
- Aho-Corasick for large suppressor lists
- User-controlled allowlists / inline ignores

title: Pack Vectorscan per-pattern metadata into AoS structs
description:
Replace separate raw_rule_ids/raw_seed_radius/raw_match_widths arrays with a single AoS (Array of Structs) for better spatial locality in vs_on_match.

## Problem
The vs_on_match callback does 3 independent pointer dereferences per hit:
- c.raw_rule_ids.add(raw_idx)
- c.raw_match_widths.add(raw_idx)
- c.raw_seed_radius.add(raw_idx)

These are separate arrays, so each access may miss cache independently.

## Solution
Pack into a single struct:
```rust
#[repr(C)]
pub struct RawPatternMeta {
    rule_id: u32,
    match_width: u32,
    seed_radius: u32,
}
// 12 bytes — 5 entries fit in one cache line
```

Single array: `raw_meta: Vec<RawPatternMeta>`

One access brings all three values into cache:
```rust
let meta = &c.raw_meta[raw_idx];
let rid = meta.rule_id;
let width = meta.match_width;
let radius = meta.seed_radius;
```

## Impact
- Reduces 3 dependent loads to 1 for the common case
- Better under dense-hit workloads where vs_on_match fires frequently

## Files to modify
- src/engine/vectorscan_prefilter.rs — define RawPatternMeta, refactor PrefilterCtx, update vs_on_match
- src/engine/core.rs — update prefilter construction

## Phase 2 — pursue if vectorscan_overhead bench shows regression or dense-hit profiles show L1 pressure
notes: Replaced split raw metadata arrays with AoS RawPatternMeta { rule_id, match_width, seed_radius } in VsPrefilterDb and callback context. vs_on_match now performs one metadata load per raw pattern id and uses fields directly. Updated callback safety/docs and prefilter scan context wiring.

title: Add value suppressors to top-5 high-FP rules
description:
Add value_suppressors_any to the five rules with the highest false-positive surface area in default_rules.yaml. Suppressors are post-regex memmem filters that discard findings where the extracted secret contains a known placeholder/example pattern.

## Background

The value suppressor gate infrastructure is fully wired (RuleSpec, RuleCompiled, YAML parsing, all four window_validate.rs paths) but no rules in default_rules.yaml currently use it. Research across TruffleHog, Gitleaks, Kingfisher, Nosey Parker, and detect-secrets identified a consensus set of high-confidence suppressor patterns that appear across multiple tools.

## High-Confidence Suppressor Patterns (from literature)

Sources: TruffleHog DefaultFalsePositives, Gitleaks DefaultStopWords, Kingfisher ignore_if_contains

**Universal (3+ tools):** example, sample, 000000, aaaaaa, xxxxxx
**Common (2 tools):** placeholder, demo, fake, abcde
**Industry standard:** REDACTED, changeme, CHANGE_ME, YOUR_, REPLACE_, INSERT_, dummy

Note: Our suppressors are case-sensitive byte memmem (not case-insensitive like Kingfisher), so both casings must be listed where needed. Short patterns like 'test' are unsafe for substring matching (hits 'latest', 'contest') — use test_ or _test instead.

## Target Rules (by FP surface area)

1. generic-api-key — broadest catch-all, highest FP rate
2. hashicorp-tf-password — generic password assignment matching
3. curl-auth-header — auth headers in curl examples/docs
4. curl-auth-user — user:pass in curl examples/docs
5. atlassian-api-token — 8 keyword anchors, broad token matching

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each rule has value_suppressors_any in default_rules.yaml
- Unit tests prove suppressors filter known placeholder values
- Integration/property tests confirm real secrets are NOT suppressed
- Benchmark or scan-level verification shows measurable FP reduction
close_reason: Completed

title: Lazy-allocate cold ScanScratch substructures
description:
Allocate large cold substructures only when needed, reducing fixed ScanScratch footprint.

## Problem
ScanScratch always allocates EntropyScratch (1284 bytes) even for rule sets with no entropy gates. Similarly, streaming/transform state is always present even for pure raw-buffer scans.

## Solution (Approach B)
```rust
// Only allocate if any rule uses entropy
entropy_scratch: Option<Box<EntropyScratch>>,  // 8 bytes when None vs 1284 bytes inline

// Only allocate if transforms are enabled
stream_state: Option<Box<StreamScratch>>,  // groups decode_ring, pending_windows, span_streams, etc.
```

Allocate on first use or at scratch initialization based on engine capabilities:
```rust
fn ensure_entropy(&mut self) -> &mut EntropyScratch {
    self.entropy_scratch.get_or_insert_with(|| Box::new(EntropyScratch::default()))
}
```

## Impact
- If no entropy rules: saves 1284 bytes per ScanScratch
- If no transforms: saves several hundred bytes of streaming state
- Pointer chase on cold use is acceptable tradeoff

## Files to modify
- src/engine/scratch.rs — wrap cold fields in Option<Box<T>>
- src/engine/window_validate.rs — update entropy_scratch access
- src/engine/core.rs — update streaming state access

## Phase 2 — only pursue if profiles show cache pressure in scratch metadata after Phase 1
notes: Implemented low-risk lazy cold allocation path: entropy_scratch is now Option<Box<EntropyScratch>> with on-demand ensure_entropy_scratch(); stream decode scratch buffers are pre-sized only when active transforms exist (minimal placeholder capacities otherwise). Updated window validation entropy accessors and memory-management docs; validated with fmt/check/clippy + targeted entropy/non-entropy engine tests.

title: Frame format v2: position-bound checksums and segment integrity
description:
Current frame format (v1) uses inline CRC-32 over type+payload only. This means misdirected writes (storage layer writes a valid frame to the wrong disk offset) pass CRC validation silently. When we add distributed replication or Tier 2 random-access indexing, this becomes a correctness problem — misattributed findings break dedup and context association.

Proposed changes for format v2:
1. Bind frame_seq (monotonic counter) and segment_id into the CRC'd region so frames at wrong positions fail checksum.
2. Add a segment trailer with frame_count, total_bytes, and a BLAKE3 hash chain over all frame checksums.
3. Chain segments within a run via prev_segment_hash in each segment header for ordering/insertion/deletion detection.
4. Bump LOG_FORMAT_VERSION to 2; reader must handle v1 (legacy) and v2.

This is a wire format breaking change — must be done before any distributed deployment. See discussion in feature/reader-recovery PR for full analysis of the TigerBeetle-style misdirected write concern.
close_reason: Implemented frame format v2 segment header/trailer integrity with prev_segment_hash chaining, replay/recovery chain verification, tests, and documentation updates.

title: Compile value suppressors into PackedPatterns and pool on Engine
description:
## Context

With `value_suppressors_any` flowing through `RuleSpec` (Task 1), we need to compile the literal patterns into the engine's optimized `PackedPatterns` format and pool them on `Engine` following the existing gate pattern.

## Goal

Compile `value_suppressors_any` into `PackedPatterns`, add a gate pool on `Engine`, and store the pool index on `RuleCompiled`.

## Scope

**In scope:**
- Add `value_suppressors: Option<PackedPatterns>` to `CompiledGates` in `src/engine/rule_repr.rs`
- Add `value_suppressors: Option<u32>` to `RuleCompiled` in `src/engine/rule_repr.rs`
- Compile suppressors in `compile_rule()`: build `PackedPatterns` from spec (raw only, no UTF-16 expansion)
- Add `value_suppressor_gates: Vec<PackedPatterns>` pool on `Engine` in `src/engine/core.rs`
- Pool each rule's compiled suppressor and patch index onto `RuleCompiled` in `Engine::new_with_anchor_policy`
- Add `value_suppressor_gate(&self, idx: Option<u32>) -> Option<&PackedPatterns>` accessor on `Engine`
- Unit tests for compilation correctness

**Out of scope:**
- Runtime evaluation in window_validate.rs (Task 3)
- No UTF-16 expansion needed — suppressors operate on extracted secret bytes (raw or decoded UTF-8)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `compile_rule()` produces correct `PackedPatterns` when `value_suppressors_any` is Some
- [ ] `compile_rule()` produces None when `value_suppressors_any` is None
- [ ] `RuleCompiled.value_suppressors` index correctly points into `Engine.value_suppressor_gates`
- [ ] Accessor returns the right `PackedPatterns` for a given index
- [ ] Unit test: compiled patterns contain expected byte sequences
- [ ] Project compiles with no warnings

## Technical Direction

- **Compilation pattern**: Follow `two_phase` compilation in `compile_rule()` but simpler — only raw patterns, no UTF-16
- Build with `PackedPatternsBuilder::with_capacity(count, raw_bytes)` then `push_raw(p)` for each pattern
- **Pooling pattern**: Follow `keyword_gates` pooling in `Engine::new_with_anchor_policy`
- **Accessor pattern**: Follow `keyword_gate()` — returns `Option<&PackedPatterns>` via `idx.map(|i| &self.value_suppressor_gates[i as usize])`
- Initialize `value_suppressors: None` in the `RuleCompiled` struct literal in `compile_rule()`, then patch in the engine constructor

title: Git findings: wire commit_id/change_kind into emitted events
description:
## Context
Git finding events in `scanner-rs` currently drop attribution context even though candidate-level context already exists in the git pipeline.

- Existing context source: `CandidateContext.commit_id` and `change_kind` (`src/git_scan/tree_candidate.rs`).
- Drop point: `stream_findings()` currently emits `commit_id: None`, `change_kind: None` (`src/git_scan/engine_adapter.rs`).
- Event model already supports these fields (`src/unified/events.rs`).

This is the highest ROI, lowest-risk attribution improvement because it reuses already-computed metadata and avoids new per-finding allocations.

## Goal
Populate `FindingEvent.commit_id` and `FindingEvent.change_kind` for git findings with near-zero overhead.

## Scope
- Thread candidate context into finding emission path in git scan adapter.
- Set `commit_id` + `change_kind` for git events only.
- Keep filesystem and non-git sources unchanged.
- Update tests for JSONL/text/sarif/event encoding expectations where needed.

## Performance Constraints
- No change to `FindingRec` layout (`src/api.rs`) or `FindingKey` layout (`src/git_scan/engine_adapter.rs`).
- No heap allocations per finding attributable to new attribution wiring.
- Preserve existing scan ordering and dedupe behavior.
- Target regression: <1% throughput change in scanner throughput benches; if >1%, include profiling evidence and mitigation.

## Implementation Notes
- Keep attribution in event layer (not core hot finding structs).
- Prefer passing compact context fields (`u32` + small enum) through existing call paths.
- Keep manual sink serialization path (no serde in hot path).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Git finding events include non-`None` `commit_id` and correct `change_kind` when available.
- FS finding events remain unchanged.
- Unit/integration tests cover git event attribution population.
- `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` passes.
- Benchmark report attached in issue notes for attribution-on path (throughput + allocation check).
notes:
Research refinement (implementation-critical):
- Prefer threading `CandidateContext` (or compact `commit_id` + `change_kind`) directly as a parameter into `stream_findings()` rather than introducing mutable adapter state like `current_ctx`.
- Rationale: same zero-allocation runtime profile, lower state complexity, easier correctness reasoning in concurrent/parallel execution paths.

title: Git findings: on-demand line/column/snippet enrichment from root offsets
description:
## Context
Current findings are offset-based (`root_hint_start/end`). Rich line/column/snippet attribution is valuable but should not degrade baseline throughput when unused.

## Goal
Add on-demand line/column/snippet enrichment only when a sink/output mode explicitly requires it.

## Scope
- Add sink capability signaling (e.g., requires line/column/snippet).
- For blobs with findings and required capability, build newline index once.
- Map sorted findings to line/column using monotonic scan over newline offsets.
- Use `root_hint_start/end` as canonical coordinate basis for consistency with transform behavior.

## Performance Constraints
- No extra line-index computation in default output modes.
- When enabled:
  - newline index built once per blob with findings
  - mapping complexity O(newlines + findings) using single forward pointer
  - avoid repeated binary search/count-per-finding patterns
- Use memchr-style scanning for newline detection to maximize throughput.

## Data-Structure/Algorithm Notes
- `Vec<u32>` newline offsets (fits current finding offset bounds, cache-friendly).
- Snippet extraction by byte-span windowing over root content; avoid forced UTF-8 normalization in hot path.
- CRLF and trailing-line edge cases must be validated.

## Correctness Notes
- Define and test line/column semantics (1-based vs 0-based) per sink format.
- Ensure snippet and coordinates remain stable with transform-derived findings where root hints are coarse/encoded.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Feature is fully gated: zero overhead path when disabled.
- Enabled mode emits correct line/column/snippet across representative fixtures (LF/CRLF, no trailing newline, binary-extractable text, transform-derived findings).
- Perf report includes overhead curve vs findings density.
notes:
Research refinement (schema safety):
- Do NOT store line/column in `FindingKey` unless a dedicated persistence/migration plan is approved.
- `FindingKey` is part of dedupe + finalize ordering semantics; changing it risks key compatibility and persistence invariants.
- Preferred approach: keep line metadata in a parallel arena/event-only extension keyed by finding span/index.
- Also note: `norm_hash` is `[u8; 32]` in this codebase, so prior size estimates assuming `u64` are invalid.
